newsitem.title: UK: Exco warns on profits, announces shake-up.
newsitem.headline: Exco warns on profits, announces shake-up.

text.p: British money broker Exco warned on Friday that a combination of quieter trading conditions and the strength of the pound would mean a sharp fall in profits in the first half of 1997.
Pre-tax profits are set to fall to around seven million pounds ($11.1 million), down from 12.1 million pounds last year.
The first half figures will also include a net restructuring provision of two million pounds to cover the costs of 154 redundancies since the start of the year.
The interim dividend is to be halved to 0.75 pence per share and unless trading improves markedly in the second half a similar cut in the full year dividend was likely, the company said.
The strength of sterling has reduced profits by some two million pounds over the first six months.
Unrelieved losses in Germany and low profitability generally will impact the group's tax charge, which for the year as a whole, is likely to exceed last year's 54 percent.
Exec shares dropped on the news, shedding 5 pence to 39 pence.
Since the beginning of the year the shares have slipped 61 percent.
In 1996 pre-tax profits were virtually flat at 18.2 million pounds and the full year dividend 4.5 pence compared to 9 pence the previous year.

At that time Exec said its strategy was to focus on securities, derivatives, capital markets and interest rate products where opportunities for profitable growth existed and to withdraw from areas where there was overcapacity and margins were thin.
Exco is now planning to integrate those products, particularly in the major financial centres of London, New York and Tokyo.
The group is also to invest 12 million pounds in new equipment and technology.
In New York, securities broking and moneybroking, previously two separate offices, are to be relocated to a new site and integrated into a single operation.
The capital cost of that move will be some six million pounds to be spent over the next six months.
The move will mean immediate savings of 1.5 million pounds annually and new technology will in time produce another one million pounds in operating efficiencies.
A 6.2 million pound provision will be made in the second half for the surrender of the leases of the existing premises and write-off of fixed assets.
A reorganisation and re-equipment programme in London will result in a further one million pound provision in the second half.
The anticipated capital cost of that is six million pounds spread over the next 2-1/2 years.
Exco has reduced broking of spot foreign exchange. it has discontinued broking of forwards in international currencies in Frankfurt and New York and reduced resources for the product in London.
The company's small Guernsey office has been closed and operations in Hong Kong have been reduced substantially. ($ = 0.628 British Pounds)
